9fba0ecb-bf98-476f-9b79-2334564b1f77: Greg Gaar’s Streets of San Francisco is a debut hardcover coffee table book of photography documenting the city’s evolving spirit, self-expression, activism, and community from the early 1970s through the early 1990s with striking intimacy and honesty. Greg will be joined in conversation by San Francisco-based photographer, filmmaker and public speaker, Jay Blakesberg. Greg Gaar’s Streets of San Francisco is the debut hard-cover coffee table book from Bay Area photographer, Greg Gaar. Spanning two transformative decades, the book documents San Francisco’s evolving spirit from the early 1970s through the early 1990s with striking intimacy and honesty. Through Gaar’s lens, fleeting moments become timeless images. The collection captures a city in motion, where bohemians, lovers, and street kids cross paths with politicians, protesters, preachers, and Pride revelers. Each photograph reflects the energy, tension, joy, and resilience that have long defined San Francisco, offering a vivid portrait of a place shaped as much by its people as by its streets. More than a photographic archive, Streets of San Francisco is a cultural document of an era when self-expression, activism, and community all collided in public space. Gaar’s rare eye and deep connection to the city result in images that feel both personal and historically essential, preserving an important chapter in San Francisco’s story. Greg Gaar (b. 1948) is a native San Franciscan, photojournalist, and environmentalist. He picked up a camera as a teenager, sharpened his eye in the Navy, then trained as a photojournalist at City College on the GI Bill before hitting the streets of San Francisco full time. He lived in Haight-Ashbury in a Queen Anne Victorian from 1896, part of a city where creative people could still afford to stay and make work. From street preachers and street musicians to the down and out, the early days of Gay Pride in SF, protests, and a healthy dose of San Francisco rock and roll, Gaar's work captures a unique moment in time in the Bay, a city that has changed dramatically since. Powerful and in your face, yet intimate, in a truly original style. This is Greg’s first coffee table book. Jay Blakesberg is a San Francisco-based photographer, filmmaker and public speaker. He has worked with legendary artists including the Grateful Dead, Neil Young, Carlos Santana, Tom Waits, Emmylou Harris and Steve Earle. His photos have been published in thousands of magazines worldwide, in numerous books, hundreds of CD packages and many documentary films. He has published 17 coffee table books of his work, including 14 under his self-publishing imprint, Rock Out Books. Jay has had three solo museum exhibitions and has photographed Hardly Strictly Bluegrass every year since 2003. www.blakesberg.com Greg Gaar - photo courtesy of the author; Jay Blakesberg - photo courtesy of Jay Blakesberg Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our SF Ferry Building store. Parties and weddings, messy hookups and marred friendships, art and love and grief— The Brightness follows the electric, chaotic, everything-can-happen lives of Pella and her best friend, Irma, as they fumble their way out of sleepy, Midwestern Westish College and into a larger world that will upend their connection and everything they thought they understood about their own place within it. At 27, Pella’s life looks settled: she’s a recent college grad, engaged to Mike, her longtime boyfriend, and helping her friend Owen pull off his own destination wedding on Block Island. But over that wild wedding weekend, Pella’s past and present collide spectacularly, blowing up her plans and sending her spiraling toward an unplanned future in New York City. Meanwhile, back at Westish College, 21-year-old Irma’s involvement with a politically charged prank—one that has roiled both the campus and the world beyond—threatens to derail her brilliant future. As Irma and Pella cycle through possibilities and identities, both navigate the heights and depths of passion and ambition, and the incalculable wages of love and loss. In stunning scenes and spectacular characters—each drawn with an almost superhuman vividness and humanity—Chad Harbach captures that specific, shimmering anxiety of your twenties when life still feels wide open, even as hard and irreversible choices start closing in. Energetic, funny, and deeply human, this much-anticipated follow-up to The Art of Fielding confirms Chad Harbach as one of the most accomplished and deep-seeing writers of our time. One of The New York Times, Chicago Review of Books, Literary Hub, and Publishers Weekly ’s Most Anticipated Books for Fall 2026 “A good book is propulsive, you can’t put it down, etc. A really good book fosters scarcity and you want to put it down as frequently as you can to live in the narrative longer. But a great book makes you feel a sort of frustration with the author that they wrote it before you. This is a good, really good, and great book. It captures a, what it was like to be a girl in college in 2016, which I was but imagine Chad wasn’t, which makes it all the more impressive, b. the complicated nature of female friendship, and c. the wonderful excruciating confusion of growing up, I could not put it down, except when I had to in order to savor it.” — Madeline Cash , author of Lost Lambs “As in his acclaimed debut, Harbach immerses readers in the world of Westish, but he broadens his scope, plunging his characters into new environments and broaching topics such as love and talent and literature, as well as campus sexual assault, feminism, the fraught politics of victimhood, and the volatile media landscape that complicates all of these. Apt evocations of Shakespeare’s The Tempest abound. While this novel can certainly be enjoyed independent of its predecessor, those who’ve read the first book will more fully appreciate the continued growth and dilemmas of Pella, Mike, and Own (the Skrimmer makes appearances, too), to say nothing of the clever metafictional twist Harbach pulls off via Owen’s novel which is titled–well, take a guess. Brilliant, poignant, and absorbing.” — Kirkus (starred) “With prose that is characteristically assured, detailed, and wise, [ The Brightness ] is sure to be the Big Cozy Read of the autumn.” — Lit Hub , Most Anticipated Books of the Year Chad Harbach is the author of the bestselling novel The Art of Fielding, which has been translated into more than twenty languages, and a founder of n+1. He was raised in Racine, Wisconsin, and educated at Harvard and the University of Virginia. He lives in Northern California with his son Ansel, and their dog, Curtis. c92e8227-266a-4a4e-b717-2a8b376f3fc0: Secret weapons and a government cover-up · An evening discussion between Pulitzer Prize winning author Lowell Bergman and the authors of "The Havana Syndrome," Michael Rey and Oriana Zill de Granados, about their book digging into a secret weapon that has baffled and confused the US public, amid years of government denial. From Havana to Tbilisi, from Vienna to Key West, the authors reveal how they spoke to the victims of Havana Syndrome attacks -- diplomats, covert intelligence officials, FBI agents and military officials -- to get the true story of what happened to them and how their government employers to this day are fighting them to hide the truth. The U.S. government fumbled its response so severely that one high-ranking former US intelligence official calls this "the biggest cover-up in my adult life." Bergman will ask the authors about their ten-year investigation at CBS News, "60 Minutes" that led to this book, and the struggles to break down the wall of classified material to get inside the investigations at CIA and the Pentagon. The authors put aside their own professional skepticism to keep digging when, over and over, they began to discover new leads the government had ignored, video evidence, eyewitness testimony about the perpetrators and internal documents placing adversaries close to known incidents. As scientists warned them that the technology was indeed possible, the authors found clues to a new type of highly specialized weapon that is both frightening and very, very real. Lowell Berman is a journalist, television producer and professor of Journalism. Bergman was a producer, reporter and director of investigative reporting at ABC News and later a producer for CBS News "60 Minutes." His investigation into the tobacco industry at "60 Minutes" was depicted in Michael Mann's movie The Insider, which was nominated for seven Academy Awards and featured Al Pacino as Bergman. From 1999 to 2008, Bergman was an investigative correspondent for The New York Times, where he was awarded the Pulitzer Prize for Public Service in 2004 for "A Dangerous Business," about worker safety and environmental law violations in the cast-iron pipe industry. Bergman was a producer and correspondent for PBS "Frontline." He founded the investigative reporting program at the Graduate School of Journalism at UC Berkeley, where he taught for 28 years. Michael Rey is an Emmy-award winning investigative producer at 60 Minutes. He has produced a series of stories about the mystery behind the Havana Syndrome, Cuban spies' networks in the United States, and Lance Armstrong's use of performance enhancing drugs, among many other long-form investigative projects. He was a senior producer for the CBS Evening News and a founding member of the CBS News Investigative Unit. He and Oriana were awarded the Alfred I. duPont/Columbia Journalism Award for their reporting on the U.S. border crisis and family separation policies. Oriana Zill de Granados has been an investigative producer for 60 Minutes since 2011. She has produced a series of stories about the mystery behind the Havana Syndrome, the mysterious deaths of the enemies of Vladimir Putin, allegations of fraud by insurance companies in Florida, scams targeting senior citizens, child separation policies of the first Trump Administration, sexual harassment in the restaurant industry, and Lance Armstrong's use of performance-enhancing drugs, among others. Her work has been awarded a duPont Award, multiple Writers' Guild and Emmy Awards, a Peabody and an IRE medal for investigative reporting.

Hiromi will be in Japan February 1-21 but will resume classes when she gets back Hiromi Vardy is a certified Zen Shiatsu, Yang style Tai Chi, and Zhineng Qigong healer and practitioner. She first encountered Tai Chi in 1973 while studying theater design and performance art in London. Initially drawn to the beauty of the movements, she soon discovered that the practice had a profound effect on her consciousness, awakening a deep interest in the healing arts. While collaborating on stage with dancers in London, Hiromi began treating injuries in overworked bodies. In 1976, after a serious accident that resulted in loss of circulation in her leg and concern about possible amputation, she turned to daily Tai Chi practice, self-massage, and treatment from a Japanese acupuncturist. This experience became a turning point in her healing journey and led her back to Japan, where she studied Shiatsu at the Namikoshi School and trained at the Zen Shiatsu Center under Shizuto Masunaga. After moving to the United States with her family in 1987, Hiromi continued deepening her practice and teaching. During a period of significant stress later in her life, she encountered Master Ming Tong Gu and began studying Zhineng (wisdom healing) Qigong under his guidance, eventually becoming licensed to teach. The healing shift she experienced through this practice was profound and continues to inform her teaching today. Since 2013, Hiromi has been dedicated to teaching Zhineng Qigong, expanding her offerings to include online classes in 2020. Her work invites students to explore the foundations of Qigong and Tai Chi as embodied, healing practices that cultivate awareness, vitality, and resilience.

1001c44e-2220-43c8-8e70-97bb9da9e52c: Some experiences change the shape of us. They leave behind questions, fragments, memories, feelings, and stories we may not always know what to do with. Sometimes, making meaning begins by giving those things somewhere to go. This gathering is an invitation to explore creative expression as a way of processing what we carry. This is a space to witness, create, and connect, and to remember that even our hardest experiences can sit alongside meaning, movement, and possibility. What to expect: We'll open with a short grounding, Nick Silva will share his story, and then make time for writing or art with prompts. Sharing is always optional. You're welcome to create quietly and just listen. No artistic experience needed. Materials will be provided. This is a peer and creative space, not therapy or crisis care. 5f0f493b-af96-4723-8fc6-e21c225868d3: Restaurateur, entrepreneur, and New York Times- bestselling author Danny Meyer reveals the secrets of his widely admired leadership philosophy and the tools he uses to build an energized, cohesive, and motivated culture. “Danny Meyer’s stories and lessons are as memorable as the flavors in his restaurants. I’ve been waiting two decades for this book, and it was worth it.”—Adam Grant, #1 New York Times bestselling author of Hidden Potential and Think Again and host of the podcast Re:Thinking NY Times article must-read! In 2006, Danny Meyer owned eleven restaurants, was nurturing a single parkside burger kiosk called Shake Shack, and had just written a bestselling book, Setting the Table, about his company’s unique culture of Enlightened Hospitality. On the first page of that book, Danny proudly declared that in twenty-five years he had never closed a restaurant. But just a few years later, he shuttered his beloved Tabla, a decision that filled him with shame—but sparked a reckoning within him about what it means to be a leader. Danny realized that his fear of failure wasn’t just misguided: it was also an impediment to his innate entrepreneurial spirit. In What Could Possibly Go Right?, he takes the reader along on his journey to learn how he’s delivered a winning culture of excellence at scale. Businesses and organizations have long understood how to scale systems of production. But it's a much trickier challenge to scale uplifting human relationships, particularly in a fluid, growing organization—one that has now spawned 700 businesses spread across twenty-four countries. As Danny writes, “Along the way, I’ve tripped and scraped my knee more times than I can count, and yet the general trajectory has been upward and to the right.” What Could Possibly Go Right? offers fascinating, lively stories from the last twenty years of Danny’s career, along with plenty of his trademark mantras (D.F.S—Don’t F’ing Settle; Change Your Grip; and Think Like a Winemaker) and leadership concepts (the Hospitality Quotient; the Rule of Two; and the Four Gears of Leadership). Together, they offer an insightful, practical, and transformative roadmap for success, yes, but more important: for making things that matter and endure. Danny believes that culture is an aspiration, not a destination. When you get your culture on the right path in any field, your missteps end up mattering far less than the innumerable lives you’ll have changed for the better. **** Danny Meyer is the New York Times bestselling author of Setting the Table, a book on his leadership philosophy of Enlightened Hospitality; the founder of Shake Shack, which he began as a hot-dog cart in Madison Square Park; and the founder of Union Square Hospitality Group (USHG), which has created some of New York’s most beloved and acclaimed restaurants, including Union Square Cafe, Gramercy Tavern, The Modern, Maialino, Eleven Madison Park, Tabla and more. He has been named a TIME 100 Most Influential Person and won the 2017 Julia Child Award; USHG has won twenty-eight James Beard Awards. Danny and his wife, Audrey, live in New York City and have four children. Danny Meyer - photo credit WaitWhat, Inc. dbd07dcf-e4d9-4067-a54c-3926adcce195: Description What becomes possible when we truly listen? This is a 2-hour introductory workshop in Imagery and Music — an experiential group practice inspired by the Bonny Method of Guided Imagery and Music (GIM), a recognized music-psychotherapy modality. You'll lie down, relax, and listen to two curated classical music programs that open space for inner imagery, emotion, and insight to surface. Then, you’ll give that experience form through simple mandala drawing. No musical or art background is needed; the only requirement is a willingness to listen. Most of the time, we listen to music. Here, we listen from inside it and music becomes less something you hear than somewhere you go. During the evening, we will: Enter a guided relaxation - Experience two curated classical music journeys - Create simple mandalas for integration — not as art, but as a way of catching what words would flatten (no experience needed) - Share reflections (optional) - Explore how Imagery and Music differs from just talking about our experiences Rather than using words, this practice lets it arrive as image, color, weight, motion — the language the psyche actually speaks. No substance is involved, only music, deep relaxation, and attention. Yet the states it opens are real: the same expanded awareness Helen Bonny first observed in psychedelic sessions, reached through sound alone. The Psychedelic Lineage: GIM was developed by Helen Bonny directly out of her work using music to support LSD-assisted therapy at the Maryland Psychiatric Research Center, where she joined the research team in 1969 alongside Stanislav Grof, Walter Pahnke, and Joan Kellogg. Bonny discovered that music, not the substance, was often the true catalyst for change. Facilitating sessions without the drug, she found that carefully selected classical music, combined with deep relaxation and verbal guidance, could open similar altered states and therapeutic imagery on its own. The mandala practice this evening traces to that same era, from Bonny's collaboration with Joan Kellogg, comparing inner imagery with the mandalas participants drew after their sessions. Today, GIM's principles are widely recognized as foundational to modern psychedelic-assisted therapy, informing how music is used to structure the arc of various psychedelic assisted therapies sessions, support emotional release, and facilitate integration. For those in the KAP and psychedelic-assisted space Whether you come as a client or a practitioner, this practice offers a structured, music-supported path for continued inner exploration and integration, between sessions, or as a standalone depth practice. This experience may resonate if you are: - Curious about music and consciousness - Seeking an experiential alternative to talk therapy - Looking for new ways to integrate mystical or non-ordinary experiences - Wanting to explore your inner world in a structured, safe way No musical background is required — only a willingness to listen. Please arrive no later than 7:10 pm. Doors will be locked to keep a safe container. *This event series honors Helen Bonny's 1973 book Music and Your Mind: Listening with a New Consciousness, the popular work that introduced her method of music-centered inner exploration. Teacher Bio: Sophia Wang is a violinist, board-certified music therapist (MT-BC), integration practitioner, and life coach whose work centers on music, imagery, and non-ordinary states of consciousness. With over a decade of clinical experience across oncology, palliative care, and mental health settings, she draws on Guided Imagery and Music, expressive arts, and depth-oriented inquiry to support emotional healing, insight, and meaningful change. Sophia works with people across a wide range of inner terrain: those in cancer care or facing the end of life; people moving through grief, depression, or anxiety; and high-performing professionals and seekers drawn to deeper self-inquiry and the integration of transformative experiences. Her approach blends clinical training with creative exploration, emphasizing safety, pacing, and integration. She holds an MA in Music Therapy from New York University and a BA in Violin Performance from Tongji University, and a Certificate in Psychedelic-Assisted Therapies and Research at the California Institute of Integral Studies (CIIS), and is an advanced trainee in the Bonny Method of Guided Imagery and Music.

4d4d519a-5293-4ec9-8ba4-72e5dc7ed8c3: Trailblazer of this generation's newfound Soul/ R&B era · Who is the man who consistently sells out all of the sophisticated & chic venues throughout North America, like City Winery, and legendary venues all around Europe like The Jazz Café in London for several consecutive nights? Dwele (pronounced dwell-lá) hails from the legendary music mecca of Detroit and lives a life in song. From stirring melodies composed on piano keys, he writes poignant music, performs with natural grace, and captivates with his clear, silky tone. He is a songwriter, producer, multi-instrumentalist, and vocalist carrying on a Motown-inspired tradition, instilled in another era. Yet Dwele has cultivated his own spirited road with five critically acclaimed albums "Subject", "Some Kinda", "Sketches Of A Man", "W.ants W.orld W.omen" and "Greater Than One" behind him. His Motor City story in sounds and upbringing resonates with genuine soul, and he's in full stride of scriting his own musical legacy. Dwele was brought up in a highly musical family that was tragically pared down to his mother and younger brother, once his father was gunned down outside their home. Dwele was only 10. ''The loss of my Father really inspired my creative side," Dwele recalls. "By getting into music, it provided me with a way to cope with his death." Dwele's music impresses with maturity beyond his years. He captures the rawness of inner city blues with hip-hop nuances that speak to his generation and beyond. His ear was shaped by Donny Hathaway, Marvin Gaye, and Miles Davis, which his family played regularly in their home. What is most compelling about Dwele's work is its timeless nature and the fact that he remains loyal to his foundation. As a multiple Grammy Award Nominee and a shared win with legendary rap icon Kanye West, he has blazed a trail for this generation's newfound Soul/ R&B era. Although being the humble young man that he is, Dwele says, " ... No matter how many Grammy nominations that I receive, I've always repped Detroit to the best of my abilities. That feeling is like exhaling, to be home while riding in the car upon my return. I see the sights, and I'm back," he muses. "When I sit down at the keyboard, as soon as I get home, the material just flows out." Dwele has toured around the globe with sold-out crowds in his wake and still seeks to mystify his audience, which makes them eagerly anticipate what his next move will be. Deemed by media queen Wendy Williams as one of "Big R&B's Best Kept Secrets", there's no doubt he has surpassed the benchmark of just getting a "Hit Record" but more so a "Hit Career." With all of that said ... It's no wonder why he was the first one chosen by McDonald's as their National Brand Ambassador for the "face and voice " of their launch of McCafe in North America. With a multitude of television appearances on Jay Leno, Jimmy Kimmel, MTV Base in Europe, and the BBC Studios Live, Dwele shows no signs of slowing. Especially since " ... He's The People's Choice," says Ronald Ron E. Estill, head of REvision/Rt Music Group, who has guided his career since inception, "it's been proven by the rave reviews for ALL of his albums." So, it's hard to even imagine when he says that "His Best is Yet to Come ... "

413af4bb-6c91-49f6-ab00-8a95b56a654e: This layered multigenerational novel follows three sisters upholding their family’s Tennessee pearl farm legacy. Rich with emotional depth and anchored by the pearl’s symbolism of beauty born from irritation, this story of resilience will captivate fans of Ann Patchett, Celeste Ng, and Claire Lombardo. Three estranged sisters—Helen, Anna, and Penn Lockshire—are bound by the shimmering but fragile legacy of their family’s freshwater pearl farm in rural Tennessee. When the business that once made them famous faces collapse, the sisters are pulled back into each other’s lives and forced to reckon with old betrayals, unspoken resentments, and the complicated truth of their inheritance. Soon, what began as a fight for survival becomes a reckoning with the myths that shaped them and the secrets buried in the family’s past. From the discovery of a rare pearl in 1981 to the struggles of a failing farm in 2008, the Lockshire sisters must navigate love, loss, ambition, and forgiveness to decide whether their heritage is a blessing to preserve—or a burden to escape. Rich with emotional depth and anchored by the pearl’s enduring symbolism—a thing of beauty born from irritation—this sweeping story of family, identity, and resilience will captivate readers of Celeste Ng and Claire Lombardo. “Gordon expertly handles her ambitious narrative and sprawling cast . . . A textured tale of renewed kinship and self-discovery.” —Kirkus Reviews “Heart-warming story of sisterhood, purpose, and family legacy.” —BookLife Reviews “ The Pearl Farmers was such a satisfying read . . . It’s an uplifting tale that resonates in these times.” —Ann Bancroft, author of Almost Family “I fell in love with Penny, Helen, and Anna, and was pulling for these three sisters to find a way back to each other. The Pearl Farmers is Yellowstone meets Little Women —but with way better jewelry!” —Emma Tourtelot, author of No One You Know Stacey Gordon grew up in the Appalachian foothills of southern Ohio and began her career as a trade journalist covering the cultured pearl and jewelry industries, visiting farms across Asia and companies around the world. For the past twenty-five years she’s worked in marketing and user experience design for the Silicon Valley tech industry. This is her debut novel. She lives with her family in Alameda, California. 0b4d665c-f0ca-424f-9b75-06be258e6a2b: A throwback to family-reads-of-yore, this epic follows a troubled boy and a host of hilariously vexed animals who must save a river before it’s dammed, so they can save themselves. Perfect for ages 10+ and all adults! School Library Journal: Review of the Day “Kirk Lombard’s The Shadow Stream is a book of great originality, a book like no other, propelled by brilliant storytelling and original thinking (and fish!) that will engage readers of all ages — a perfect family book.” — Mark Kurlansky, author of Cod and Salt and World Without Fish Gabriel (“G” for short) is wasting away in the Abiddon County Juvenile Center when he’s introduced to the Shongunk River by his dying uncle. The river valley — trash-heaped but chock-full of mysteries and fish — wins G over. But, as G has learned, good things can’t last. The Shongunk is scheduled to be dammed by a local developer. In a matter of days, it will cease flowing, and all of the talkative creatures who live in the river valley will be as homeless as G. Just as G decides it’s no time to accept his fate, so too do the animals. To inspire an uprising, a young trout is nominated to make a fateful journey up the river; a raccoon swears a violent oath against humans; and a newly sober buck leads his skittish flock out of harm’s way. Together with G, they show there is power in all of us, even the smallest minnow. Kirk Lombard is an author, angler, sustainable fishmonger and tuba player who worked inside the juvenile rehabilitation system. His first book, the award-winning Sea Forager’s Guide to the Northern California Coast , was described as “poetry” for fish, by NPR. He lives in the Bay Area with his family, raising his children on herring and sea shanties. 5895be96-05df-43cc-92de-d5c19c3c22bb: What if sound is something you felt in the body as much as heard in your ears? Long before it was music, sound served as medicine, prayer, and portal — a technology for shifting consciousness that predates language itself. Join Grammy-nominated artist and teacher Radhika Vekaria for an immersive afternoon built around direct, felt experience: exploring mantra and the intelligence of sound through your own body, breath, and voice. Through direct practice and philosophical insight, this session works with sound as an organizing intelligence, one that refines focus, strengthens presence, and cultivates inner coherence. This is active work: chanting, mudras, and breath practice done together as a group. You will explore: - The relationship between sound and resilience - The deeper meaning behind mantra - Chant as a practice of clarity and courage - Mudra and Nāda yoga as embodied extensions of the practice Rooted in yogic philosophy and grounded in contemporary life, this immersion offers an approach to cultivating steadiness, awareness, and peace. No prior experience is required. The afternoon closes with a 75-minute live performance with Radhika singing in a communal setting, drawing on the same deep lineage that guides the whole workshop. Teacher Bio: Radhika Vekaria is a Grammy®-nominated artist and composer working at the crossing point of Sanskrit and Vedic sacred sound and contemporary music. Her voice draws on devotional and contemporary vocal styles as well as Hindustani classical tradition — she studied for several years under Meher Paralikar, a disciple of Padma Bhushan Pandit Ajoy Chakrabarty of the Patiala-Kasur gharana — alongside classical piano trained since childhood. That grounding shows up in every performance: precise, disciplined, and unmistakably rooted in lineage, even as the music itself moves into new territory. Her project SAPTA: The Seven Ways, an exploration of Vedic mantra, became a healing practice for everyone who encountered it, and made her the first mantra artist to perform at SXSW in 2022. Her 2025 album Warriors of Light earned a Grammy nomination and extended that same inquiry into how ancient sound moves through a contemporary ear. Named after Radha, the Vedic symbol of devotion, she treats sacred sound as a living practice — one she has carried from concert stages to sacred gatherings across the globe. Radhika has performed at Harvard, Omega Institute, the Grammy Museum, and prestigious venues like Estelle Manor and Naviva, reflecting the wide lens through which she is able to convey this wisdom and reach people. Growing up in a British East African Indian family, Radhika was immersed in Vedic rituals since childhood. Learning music from early infancy and with continuous exploration of the multiple arenas of Vedic traditions and philosophy, she has a refreshing approach to how this wisdom can be imbibed and applied in the world today. In 2022, her live audio rooms online reached over 100,000 people with meditation and mantra sessions. She offers a room an experience of return — voice and mantra used deliberately to move people from thinking into feeling, from the head to the heart. That instinct shapes both her performances and her workshops: through similar sessions, she works directly with people's own relationship to sound and voice, drawing on the same tradition and training behind her stage work. For a space built around inquiry and embodied practice, she brings a performance to be moved by, and a practice to be moved through. Explore more at www.radhikavekaria.com

4425820a-7b08-4636-aedb-4133a4f1159e: Andrea Brewster, Draft 1, 2026, giclee print, woven vellum, 10″ x 10″, photo courtesy of the artist Andrea Brewster’s new body of work, Draft, begins with the fundamental structure of weaving: warp and weft, whose interlacing creates both fabric and an underlying grid. She approaches the grid not as a rigid system, but as a living structure capable of variation, interruption, rhythm, and ambiguity. The work draws from weaving drafts, diagrams that function as instructions for generating complex patterns, resembling a form of pre-digital code. The term “draft” also refers to an initial idea or work in progress, connecting structure with imagination and instruction with image.This connection between weaving and digital systems is central to Brewster’s thinking. Although digitally constructed, these pieces retain the appearance of hand-drawn marks, creating a tension between material and virtual, order and improvisation. Through line, color, repetition, and interruption, Brewster explores the relationship between visible patterns and the structures beneath them. Bio: Andrea Brewster is a multidisciplinary artist who investigates the intersection of nature, fiber art, and technology through intricate forms and layered textures. Brewster earned a B.A. in Sculpture from Pomona College and an M.F.A. in New Genres from the San Francisco Art Institute. A 1993 NEA grant recipient, she has exhibited widely in the San Francisco Bay Area, with solo shows at Mercury 20, The Lab, and Southern Exposure, as well as group exhibitions at Metal Haus Gallery, Chandra Cerrito Contemporary, The Oakland Museum, and the Peninsula Museum. Her work has been featured in fiber art exhibitions in Ireland and the U.S. She has participated in the Djerassi Resident Artist Program, and in 2025, her AI work appeared at Load Gallery, Barcelona, and in the book Neo Botanica. She has been a member of Mercury 20 Gallery since 2020. bbc0f6b3-54cc-4ef5-b10e-2262ff88de9d: Jill McLennan, Walter, 900 years old, watercolor, collage, ink, 26″x20″. photo by artist Jill McLennan’s work gives voice to the harmless, reflecting on the federal government’s decision to rescind the definition of harm (2026) as it applies to the protection of animals and their habitats, listed under the Endangered Species Act (1975). In her art, she depicts animals adapting, inventing new ways to thrive amidst human impact. Using sumi ink, a brush, and mulberry paper, she paints mammals, birds, amphibians, plants, trees, and rivers. Then, tearing the paper, she applies these images to wood panels. Adding watercolor and handmade paper, she creates a transformation from reality to wonder. McLennan states, “The animals are here alongside us, they have always been here, and it is our duty to ensure that they remain, that their habitat is here on earth for generations to come. May my art be a message to harm less, a cry to the present and a hope for the future.” Bio: Jill McLennan creates paintings, collages and prints inspired by her surroundings and the stories that she collects. She has been a member of Mercury 20 Gallery since 2007. She is an active member of her neighborhood, Jingletown Arts, Business + Community (JABC), organizing Open Studios as well as beautification projects. She recently printed a series of linoleum blocks with poems, telling stories of migration and climate change, through a residency at the Kala Art Institute in Berkeley, CA. McLennan has completed two public art projects: Jingletown Birds at 401 Derby and Emeryville Perspectives at 65th and Christie Streets. Both are cut steel fences depicting the local shoreline with birds, designed by McLennan and executed by local metal fabricators. Her work was accepted to the deYoung Open in 2020 and 2023. As an artist and teacher, she is deeply invested in protecting her environment, inspiring the youth, and spreading hope and joy into the world. 43328855-405d-4b2d-9659-93f3b27d21b4: (Please do not bring infants to the show) Born into a radical theater company, Joyful Raven was tasked from the tender age of 5 with the daunting mission to save the world from impending doom… using theater. Forced into animal-print unitards and political positions long before she was a consenting adult, she never had a fighting chance at anything resembling a normal life. You think your parents were embarrassing? Did you have to sing about salmon sex on stage, in a unitard, at 12 years old… WITH your parents? I didn’t think so. In an attempt to heal her hippie trauma, she runs away from home to seek solace in the arms of a spiritual teacher… and accidentally finds herself in the yoga-to-fascism pipeline. Can she save herself? Can she save the world… using theater?! Blending standup, drag, storytelling, & clown, Raven takes audiences on a dystopian and hilarious romp through the looking glass. ACTOR : Joyful Raven is an award-winning actor, director, and “story midwife” known for her powerful and thought-provoking solo shows, where she tackles thorny social issues with humor, heart, and nuance. Born into an iconic political theater family, she has been devising original work for over 20 years. Her first solo comedy, Tales of a Sexual Tomboy , was dubbed “…one of the funniest shows now on display on Bay Area stages” by the SF Chronicle, won Best of the Fringe at the 2016 San Francisco International Fringe Festival, and enjoyed an Off-Broadway run in 2017. Her latest solo show, Breed or Bust , was nominated for Best Comedy at the 2022 Hollywood Fringe Festival, critically acclaimed at the 2023 Edinburgh Fringe, where it won an Offie (OffWestEnd Award), and went on to have an extended run at The Marsh, where it received a Critics’ Pick in the SF Chronicle. She co-founded the award-winning theater company Rococo Risqué and co-authored four plays for the Prize of Hope-winning company Human Nature. As an actor, she has appeared in numerous stage and film projects, including Odyssey Works, the film The Pursuit of Happyness alongside Will Smith, and Spring Awakening, directed by Stafford Arima. Joyful holds an MFA in Dramatic Art from the University of California, Davis, and teaches solo performance and storytelling at Berkeley Rep School of Theatre, The Marsh, and her own studio in Berkeley. Lynne Kaufman ( Playwright ) is the author of 20 full-length plays that have been produced in San Francisco, Los Angeles, Washington D.C., and Louisville at such theatres as Magic Theatre, Actors Theatre of Louisville, TheatreWorks Silicon Valley, and many more –with Shameless Hussy being her most recent work which premiered at The Marsh San Francisco spring 2025. Four of Kaufman’s plays, Extreme Acts, Acid Test, Two Minds , Who Killed Sylvia Plath , and Poetic Justice, have premiered on stage at The Marsh, while two others, Exposing Margaret Mead and The Smartest Woman in America, have appeared on The Marsh’s digital platform MarshStream. 8acc4dd7-eadb-4cc3-9de8-6f70c06acf9d: Mothers and Daughters: Writing Formative Relationships in Memoir What does it mean to reckon with the past and find yourself on the other side? In this panel, three She Writes Press memoirists, Robin Rosenbluth, Georgine Hodgkinson, and Rosanne Annoni, explore the profound and complicated ways their mothers shaped them, and the unexpected journeys that led each of them home to herself. From a young white woman navigating the semi-nomadic communities of 1970s Kenya while carrying the wounds of the U.S. foster care system, to a spiritual seeker tracing the long arc between a childhood vision of Christ and a solitary winter at Gampo Abbey, to a college professor who upended her carefully controlled life for the wilds of Puerto Rico's cryptocurrency scene, these are stories of displacement, desire, and hard-won transformation. Moderated by She Writes Press publisher Brooke Warner, this panel is an invitation to explore those moments that break us open and the unlikely places where healing takes root. Each of these memoirs reminds us that growing up isn't something that happens only in childhood, and that our mothers, for better or worse, are the first maps any of us is given to navigate ourselves and our lives. Robin Rosenbluth is a former foster teen who advocates for finding permanent homes for older foster youth. She has worked in the nonprofit sector in New York as a fundraiser, an adjunct professor at Columbia University and New York University. She has studied memoir and the craft of writing with many renowned authors and writes a Substack, My Jagged Journey as a Debut Writer . Robin and her wife have raised two children who now have families of their own. She lives in Brooklyn, New York. Rosanne Annoni was a successful psychotherapist for thirty-five years in the Bay Area before becoming an ordained teacher of the Diamond Approach in 2000. She has taught students and mentored teachers in the United States, the UK, and the EU. In 2024, she was awarded an Emerging Writer Fellowship from Aspen Words. She is married, has one son, and lives with her husband and dog on Cape Cod. Georgine Hodgkinson is a professor of communication studies at Cosumnes River College in Sacramento, where she also served as program coordinator for Re-Emerging Scholars, a program for formerly incarcerated students. Her published scholarship includes book chapters, journal articles, and essays exploring politics, gender, and spirituality. In 2025, she was a People’s Choice Winner for the Amy MacRae International Memoir Award. A certified yoga instructor who loves to run and play pickleball, Georgine splits her time between Dorado, Puerto Rico, and Folsom, California, with her husband, Mark. Brooke Warner is publisher of She Writes Press, a memoir coach, and author of Write On, Sisters!, Green-light Your Book, What's Your Book?, and three books on memoir. She’s a TEDx speaker, weekly podcaster (of “Write-minded” with co-host Grant Faulkner of NaNoWriMo), and publishes a weekly newsletter, Writerly Things, on Substack at brookewarner.substack.com . db847257-cf52-42e0-a7b6-d0b015bca9ae: Prize-winning historian Kevin Waite uncovers an extraordinary story of survival in this first book-length biography of Biddy Mason. The narrative follows Mason's journey from the cotton South to metropolitan California, detailing how she crossed the continent, broke free from slavery, and built Black Los Angeles. Through the lens of the Civil War, Reconstruction, and the dawn of Jim Crow, Waite reveals Mason's profound impact on California's history. Los Angeles’s leading Black property owner entered the city as a piece of property herself. Born enslaved in 1818, Biddy Mason was forcibly transported 3,000 miles to California before winning her freedom in a landmark 1856 court case. By the time of her death, she had become one of the wealthiest African Americans in the West – an entrepreneur, philanthropist, and founding mother of Black Los Angeles. The Boundless Biddy Mason: An Odyssey from Slavery to Freedom Across the American West, Kevin Waite’s masterful biography of Mason – the first full-length study of her extraordinary life – places Mason at the center of a larger American story: the expansion of slavery into the West, the legal battles that tested freedom’s meaning, and the rise of a vibrant Black Los Angeles community she helped build. Waite documents Mason’s early years in Mississippi and follows her forced journey across the continent, as one of roughly 1,500 enslaved African Americans who were trafficked from the slave states to the frontier. Her enslaver, Robert Smith, a convert to Mormonism, marched Mason and her children from Mississippi to Utah and ultimately to California. Despite the state’s constitutional ban on slavery, Smith became the largest slaveholder in California, with fourteen people under his control. But it wasn’t until Smith attempted to relocate his human chattel to Texas that the law intervened. A pitched legal battle in Los Angeles resulted in freedom for Mason, her three daughters, and ten other women and children. From that moment forward, Mason reshaped her destiny – and the destiny of her city. She built a respected practice as a nurse and midwife, invested shrewdly in downtown real estate, cultivated influential alliances, and helped found Southern California’s first Black church. Her canny ability to disarm her denigrators with kindness and competence earned Mason a reputation as a leader. Award-winning historian Kevin Waite ably connects Mason’s life to the nation’s great upheavals: the westward expansion of slavery, the Civil War and Reconstruction, and the dawn of Jim Crow. In doing so, he restores Mason to her rightful place in American history, detailing her role as a survivor of forced migration, a litigant in a landmark freedom suit, and an architect of Black Los Angeles. Mason’s legacy in Los Angeles endures to this day, not only as founding member of the First African Methodist Episcopal Church but also in the public works she inspired. “In this astute work of historical recovery, Kevin Waite has provided us with a definitive, modern biography of the remarkable Biddy Mason…a tremendous achievement and a cautionary tale for our own fraught times.” ―Manisha Sinha, author of The Rise and Fall of the Second American Republic: Reconstruction, 1860–1920 “Combining meticulous scholarship with taut, propulsive prose, Kevin Waite tells the story of how the quietly extraordinary Biddy Mason helped break slavery's hold on Southern California. Absorbing and revelatory, this is history at its best.” —Nathaniel Philbrick, National Book Award–winning author of In the Heart of the Sea and The Rush “Kevin Waite has written the book we’ve needed for a long time. Biddy Mason was a most extraordinary woman. With great care and exhaustive research, Kevin Waite has written her biography as part of the stories of enslavement and emancipation as well as faith and community at the western edge of the United States.” —Kelly Lytle Hernández, author of Bad Mexicans Kevin Waite is Anne Stark Watson and Chester Watson Distinguished Professor of History at the University of Texas at Dallas. His first book, West of Slavery , won the 2022 Wiley-Silver Prize and was shortlisted for three other awards, including the Lincoln Prize. His writing appears in The Atlantic , the Los Angeles Times , The Washington Post , Slate , National Geographic , and The New Republic . Kevin moonlights in the TV and film industry, most recently as the writer and producer of a six-episode docuseries on the American Revolution for National Geographic and Disney+. 48e17d40-b720-4d33-973e-b298addffc76: Lucid dreaming is not reserved for the special few. Rather, it is a trainable skill, and a doorway into the deeper practice of psychonavigation, the art of moving through your own psyche with clarity, intention, and skill. In this workshop, mother-daughter teaching team Norma Burton and Nisha Burton will guide participants through foundational practices that many cultures throughout history have used to work with dream and the subconscious. Participants will be introduced to lucid dreaming as an accessible, learnable practice, along with complementary inner pathways like dreamwork, shadow work, and drumming journeys. Together, these tools can help build a working map of one's own inner world, supporting healing, sharpening intuition, and strengthening the kind of discernment that can be very useful in a world saturated with noise and division. The workshop is also intended as a foundation for anyone preparing for or integrating psychedelic experiences, offering grounded skills for navigating altered states. During the workshop, participants can expect to: - Learn the fundamentals of lucid dreaming and how to begin cultivating it through simple, evidence-informed techniques - Explore dreamwork and shadow work practices for interpreting dreams and identifying unconscious patterns - Begin building a personal practice, starting with dream journaling, to carry these tools into daily life - Learn both beginning and advanced lucid dreaming techniques Rooted in nearly thirty years of Norma's work in Buddhist practice, Jungian shadow work, and trauma healing, and brought into the present through Nisha's own experience with lucid dreaming, this workshop offers an intergenerational approach to teaching — practical, embodied, and grounded in decades of lived experience. Website: luciddreaminglucidliving.com Instagram: @lucid_dreaming_lucid_living Teacher Bios: Norma J. Burton is a pioneering expert in complex trauma healing with over 40 years of counseling experience. She did M.A. and Ph.D. work at Berkeley's Graduate Theological Union, and M.Div. at Pacific School of Religion with specializations in Hospice Chaplaincy and Psychology. Her distinguished career began with a decade of leadership in domestic violence advocacy, where she served as Director of battered women's shelters around the country, before serving at the National Coalition Against Domestic Violence headquarters. In the early 1990s, Burton developed the Journey to Completion™, an innovative spiritual-psychological, trauma healing process now practiced internationally. Building on this foundation, she founded and directed The Circle of Trust Healing Center in 2014, a state-certified addiction recovery and mental health facility. Under her leadership, the center conducted groundbreaking studies demonstrating the superior effectiveness of holistic approaches in achieving lasting addiction recovery. Burton's unique blend of academic rigor, clinical expertise, and innovative methodology has positioned her at the forefront of transformative healing practices. Nisha Burton is a lucid dreaming practitioner, award-winning filmmaker, and emerging technologies consultant. Raised in a shamanic lineage, she grew up traveling the world as a child to study directly with wisdom keepers. She carries ancestral knowledge of altered states and soul work passed through Choctaw, Santee, and Cree lines, a Yoruba lineage rooted in her father's work, and a Druidic thread on her mother’s Celtic side. From an early age, she was steeped in the disciplined art of navigating one's own psyche with skill - above all through staying impeccable by doing the deep, ongoing work of shadow integration. This lineage-rooted foundation shapes how she guides others through altered states today. Along with linage based knowing she has also extensively studied Tibetan Dream Yoga, Jungian Dream Analysis, and dream researchers such as Stephen LaBerge. As co-founder of Lucid Living Inc., she delivers Lucid Dreaming workshops globally. Nisha has co-authored three books on consciousness exploration: Navigating Liminal Realms (Findhorn), Lucid Dreaming Lucid Living (Red Wheel/Wieser), and The Psychonaut's Oracle (Schiffer). She speaks internationally on consciousness navigation and AI innovation.

b7c8e18f-3631-41d3-81cf-da0d00ba0a6e: Two-Way Mirror books celebrates the release of its latest books: Danny Rosen ‘s A Love Poem Called War and J Grabowski ‘s POMPEI: or The Notes Are In The World , with music by J Lee’s Starry Skemes . Publisher Marina Lazzara hosts. Each morning Danny Rosen pees on the bank of the largest unnamed tributary to the East Branch of Big Salt Wash which flows into the Colorado River several miles below Fruita, Colorado. Early on he learned to swing a hammer and that changed everything. He has been a poet, publisher, teacher, geologist, astronomer, and carpenter. In the middle of his journey he found himself running an astronomical observatory in the heart of the Namib Desert under the southern sky where he cultivated an optimistic outlook based on his familiarity with big space and deep time. He is the author of Suspended Erosion (2024), The Tuscan Journals & Other Poems (2022), Primate Poems (2016), Ghosts of Giant Kudu (2013), and That Curve (2006). He founded Lithic Press in 2007 and has run Lithic Bookstore since its opening in 2015. An inveterate rock hanger, he has collaborated with beavers on a variety of landscape installations. J Grabowski is an artist from New York whose practice explores drawing, writing, painting, sculpture, movement, and music. He cofounded PUSH Press, the Heliopolis Project (2010-2015), POMPEI and Turtle Records. Previous publications include Time Landscape (Bird & Beckett, 2017). J.Lee is a San Francisco is a San Francisco multi instrumentalist, songwriter, improviser, modular synthesist and visual artist. He is a member of the indie psych rock band Starry Skemes and the experimental rock band Warm Spell. He has formerly played with the Rabbles, Static Faction and Aerosol Species.

672f901f-a899-4079-b9e5-cf22ee3c1ff5: October Theme: “Broadway and Show Tunes” There’s nothing that brings people together better than singing our favorite songs. It recalls summer nights around the campfire: someone strumming the guitar and all singing a mix of folk music, familiar songs we heard on the radio, and occasional new songs that someone shares. Nobody has to worry about whether you know the songs or can sing like a pro. This is our chance to share the joy of singing simply for the fun of it. Cary Sheldon is a singer, songwriter, and beloved Berkeley voice teacher with 30 years worth of grateful students. She has been playing and teaching in the Bay Area for the last 40 years. Her love for R & B music led her to be part of Zazu Pitts Memorial Orchestra in the 1980’s. Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. She continues to be inspired by her love of singing in community. “Singing together with others is one of the greatest joys in my life.” Now in her 60’s, she returns to influences from her early life. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. She hopes to inspire others to explore the depth of this material and rediscover the joy of community singing. Soprano Candace Johnson has led AMN’s Juneteenth Choral Celebration since its inception in 2020. The AMN community knows her through her commitment to the power of the Negro Spirituals tradition, but Candace has a deep connection to theater and to the music of the Broadway stage. A voice instructor at UC Berkeley for 17 years, in 2022 Candace also became the director of the University Gospel Choir. A lyric coloratura soprano, she crosses musical boundaries performing classical, jazz, musical theater, pop and gospel. She has sung on many stages, including Carnegie Hall and The Manhattan Center. Also a playwright and actress, Candace premiered her first one-woman show, Vox in a Box , in UC Berkeley’s Hertz Hall in 2018, which led to her becoming a resident solo artist at The Marsh theater (Berkeley/San Francisco). Candace has written and performed 5 full-length one-woman musicals. Her most recent show, Scat-ter Brain: The Music of ADHD , was commissioned by The Marsh in 2024 for its inaugural IFOYE festival of new works by women-identifying playwrights. ab3e9468-7867-46e3-8440-466e4412988b: Every Tuesday morning, the Alembic opens for a half-day of silent meditation practice. This is an unguided silent retreat consisting of three 40-minute meditation periods. There will be no teacher-led instruction during the meditation periods. Participants are invited to bring and engage in their own silent meditation practice. Whether you practice mindfulness, Zen, Vipassana, contemplation, prayer, or another silent form of meditation, all are welcome. The retreat begins promptly at 9:30 AM and concludes at 11:50 AM. Please arrive between 9:15 AM and 9:25 AM to remove your shoes, settle in, and find a seat before the first bell. The morning is divided into three periods of silent meditation: 9:30 AM – 10:10 AM 10:20 AM – 11:00 AM 11:10 AM – 11:50 AM A bell will signal the beginning and end of each meditation period. The meditation hall (Sol) is reserved for silent practice during sitting periods. Between sits, participants may quietly stretch, visit the restroom, or spend time in the tearoom. Conversation is permitted during breaks; however, we encourage participants to keep voices low, as some attendees choose to observe silence throughout the entire morning. You are welcome to leave the meditation hall at any time if needed. If you leave during a meditation period, please wait until the next break before re-entering. We ask that all entrances and exits be as quiet and unobtrusive as possible. This is a “Bring Your Own Silent Meditation” retreat. We provide the structure and the space; you provide your own silent practice. Participants may choose to sit in Sol or engage in quiet movement practice in the tearoom during meditation periods. To minimize disruption, please enter Sol only during the transition periods between sits. If you arrive after a meditation period has begun, you are welcome to practice elsewhere in the Alembic until the next bell. The suggested donation is $10. No one will be turned away for lack of funds. We do ask that all attendees register through the Momence app or via the registration link on the Alembic website. Please note that the retreat ends at 11:50 AM, and we ask all participants to depart by 12:00 PM so that our volunteer teacher and staff may close the space in a timely manner. Thank you for helping us maintain a quiet and supportive environment for practice.

4dcc3918-7d7b-42ef-844a-edeb09f4f42c: Crisis leadership can be the toughest type of leadership—and the most crucial to master. 21cc06b4-b345-4ae4-becc-1eaeb4787d94: Join us at Books Inc. Campbell to celebrate author Scott Lambridis on the debut of his first novel, St. Ulphia’s Dead ! About the Book Disgraced medical researcher Mirs and his skeptical new supervisor Jo arrive on the remote island of St. Ulphia to investigate an outbreak of mass psychosis. The villagers claim they’re being possessed— one by one— by a cannibalistic demon known as the Wendigo. While unraveling the villagers’ strange tales, Mirs and Jo are drawn into a tangle of local politics, mysterious disappearances, and impossible contradictions. When the missing begin to reappear, the boundaries between fact and folklore become dangerously thin. As tensions rise and trust fractures, Mirs and Jo must confront the possibility that the madness around them may not be entirely imagined— or may not be the villagers’ alone. A psychological mystery laced with absurd humor, St. Ulphia’ s Dead explores how trauma warps truth, how isolation breeds belief, and how the most terrifying demons are the ones we conjure for ourselves. About the Author Born and raised in New York, Scott earned a degree in neurobiology from the University of Virginia. He’s toured the Midwest with a progressive rock band, founded an indie press and performance series, earned an MFA from San Francisco State University, tended a 40-acre olive farm, and read a book from every country of the world. He wrote St. Ulphia’s Dead during his daughter’s naps during a year in France, and finally settled with his wife and child in Bellingham, Washington, “the city of subdued excitement.”
2868b2e6-6cda-439e-b07b-32e712ff9895: Following the car accident that ended his football career and left his body scarred, twenty-two-year-old Luke Griffin joins the cast of Endeavor , a new competition-based reality show that pits the tabloids' darlings against one another in tasks of endurance and problem solving. At first, he thrives, effortlessly forming friendships and even a romantic relationship that he thinks will last a lifetime. But Luke has aspirations far bigger than the show's million-dollar prize, and soon a series of betrayals leads to irreversible tragedy, changing the course of his and his fellow contestants' lives forever. Ten years later, Luke's world looks very different: He is now a father of two and the stay-at-home husband to America's only openly gay senator. When his husband's serial cheating is exposed, Luke impulsively joins the cast of Endeavor 's latest season in a desperate bid to earn some fast cash. Back on set, he is confronted with everything he tried to leave in the past: bitter rivalries, shattered friendships, and crushing guilt, all of which threaten to tear down the walls he's spent a decade building. As Season 20 of Endeavor kicks off, Luke must give everything to the game, even as he finally learns what it means--and what it costs--to face the truth. ​Combining the fabulous rivalries of The Traitors with the epic physical stunts of The Challenge , The Book of Luke offers a grounded portrait of what it means to reinvent yourself when no one will let you forget your past--especially if it's immortalized on streaming services.

ff498187-2091-4f15-88c4-01a7bf9ce7bd: A group meditation/authentic relating practice that explores what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to each other Welcome to a twice-monthly drop-in Relatefulness practice with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli. Relatefulness is an exploration of what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to the others in the group. It is a close friend of relational practices like Circling™, Authentic Relating, and T-Group, with slightly more emphasis on group interaction and flexibility in how to express what is arising in the present moment. This is a mixed-levels event. Beginners are welcome and will be supported with tools to aid their exploration. Advanced practitioners will be challenged to find the next edge of their practice. We cap attendance for the event at 15 people. If you want to be sure to be able to join, purchase your ticket in advance! What We’ll Explore Through paired, small group, and full group processes, we will practice: Noticing and naming the content of our experience, including: our emotions, body sensations, and present moment reactions to others in the group. Noticing and naming the context of our experience, including: our assumptions, the norms of the group, and projections onto one another and society. Revealing our experience to one another to help all of us see each other and our broader social reality more clearly. Leading the group in the direction we want to go. This is a practice where all participants are invited to notice their desires for the group and to practice directing the group by embodying the kinds of expression they want to see more of. Why Come? You may be looking to: Cultivate more authentic, nourishing relationships, where you can be yourself and stay connected. Take your insights about personal growth and explore them in an interpersonal context. Set clear, compassionate boundaries instead of repeating painful patterns This practice helps to develop skills that support all of the above. Also, it's fun! What Not to Expect This is not a therapy session or group healing experience, although healing can occur. It’s a group exploration of what is arising in the present moment. This naturally tends to bring out more truth and love in the group, but there is not a particular goal or endpoint we are trying to reach. Here’s what NOT to expect: A space free of conflict or triggers. When people are open about what's coming up in their experience, things can get edgy sometimes! We don’t view being triggered as inherently negative, but rather a natural part of the human experience that can be rich to explore. We aim for a space where safety grows from honesty and genuine care, not from avoiding interpersonal conflict. To support this, we will establish some boundaries up front, such as asking for explicit consent before making physical contact with others. No enforced hierarchy of emotions. Beauty, awkwardness, boredom, anger, and joy are all welcome. Each experience has worth, and none automatically justify themselves as more important. Expression without attunement. We value honest expression, and we also stay attentive to its impact on others. This is a space for mindful connection, not expression at any cost. Facilitators may pause or redirect moments that move away from relational presence. Other logistics and notes Participants enter the space at 6:30 and we close the doors for the event at 6:35. Please arrive on time! We hope to see you at a future event! Feel free to reach out to jhrosenberg [at] gmail [dot] com or dbricciardelli [at] gmail [dot] com if you have questions about whether this event is a fit for you. More about the facilitators Josh Rosenberg (he/him) is a certified facilitator through the Relateful Company training program. He has hosted and facilitated weekly relatefulness sessions for small groups for several years while continuing to grow his practice through retreats and regularly engaging other facilitators. Josh loves exploring what's honestly coming up in the present moment in a group of people, and the novelty and relief it tends to bring. When he's not leading relatefulness sessions or at work, you may find him loving the heck out of music, movies, and comedy, participating in Michael Taft's meditation courses, or passionately following the New York Jets football team despite its many flaws. 4062dd46-ca7d-47af-b089-284e2b45f3fd: One of today’s premier jazz drummers · "The Groove Master", Herlin Riley is widely considered one of the best drummers in any genre of music performing today. The longtime drummer for the legendary Ahmad Jamal and the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra now leads two groups, his quintet and the New Orleans Groove Masters featuring himself, Jason Marsalis, and Shannon Powell. Herlin’s most recent album, Perpetual Optimism, reunites the quintet of rising stars that Riley assembled for his Mack Avenue Records debut, New Direction. Since the release of that acclaimed album, all four of Riley’s bandmates – trumpeter Bruce Harris, saxophonist Godwin Louis, pianist Emmet Cohen, and bassist Russell Hall – have been making major waves across the modern jazz scene, attesting to the master drummer’s Art Blakey-like ear for talent and sage musical guidance. Herlin Riley's source of strength comes from his faith in God, his wife of four decades, and his family of five children and 10 grandchildren; his lifelong home in New Orleans, the creative community that surrounds it, and his positive approach to life and music. His roots in the church are also vital, shining through in the congregational claps that help establish the celebratory spirit that is showcased in the album opener “Rush Hour.” He also relies on his musical family, including his long-established ties with Wynton Marsalis and the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra. Riley’s connection to the Marsalis dynasty traces back a generation earlier, to family patriarch and fellow lifelong New Orleanian Ellis Marsalis. It was while performing with Ellis at the annual New Orleans Jazz and Heritage Festival in a trio with bassist Reginald Veal that Riley first caught the ear of Wynton, who invited both members of his father’s rhythm section to join him, launching a vital relationship that’s now lasted more than three decades. Riley pays homage to his mentor on the closing track of Perpetual Optimism, the funky arrangement of Ellis Marsalis’ composition “Twelve’s It.” In the quintet’s lively rendition, the tune is not just a cover but a tribute, as Riley intones a short ode to passing the torch that refers to the elder Marsalis as “a great musician who taught a whole lot of fellows.” Another Crescent City icon, the late singer, pianist, songwriter, and producer Allen Toussaint, was the motivator behind Riley’s other vocal turn on the album, a gritty take on Willie Dixon’s blues classic “Wang Dang Doodle.” Toussaint stopped in to hear Riley play at a New Orleans club and heard the drummer’s 5/4 arrangement of the familiar standard. “He was really impressed,” Riley recalls. “He said, ‘Wow, man, I’ve heard ‘Wang Dang Doodle’ a thousand times, but I’ve never heard it performed in 5 before. You should record that.’ A few months later, he passed away, so I recorded the tune to pay homage to the wishes of the great Allen Toussaint.” Though he conveys vivid emotion in his voice, Riley stops short of calling himself a singer. His willingness to step to the mic comes from advice he was given by New Orleans vocal great Germaine Bazzle. “She’s a very elegant and regal lady, but when she’s performing, she scats, rolls her shoulders, dances, and really engages in the music with honesty and passion,” says Riley. When he asked her how she reconciled those two extremes, Bazzle told him, “’ You have to allow yourself to become emotionally naked when you’re on the bandstand.’ When she said that, a light bulb went off in my head. I’m not a singer, but I just do what I do, and I have the audacity to be uninhibited.” The same can be said for Riley’s work behind the kit, where he leads his stellar band with infectious enthusiasm and bristling swing. His “Be There When I Get There” captures the anticipation and excitement of rushing to an eagerly awaited appointment, whether a romantic rendezvous, a gathering of friends, or a night of music. The brisk “Borders Without Lines” comes from the pen of Riley’s Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra bandmate Victor Goines, while the classic “You Don’t Know What Love Is” becomes a sultry simmer, highlighted by Harris’ mournful, muted trumpet. The title track is the rare Riley original composed in a major key, and its sunny disposition perfectly communicates his unflagging hopefulness. The lovely “Touched,” featuring Louis’ achingly lyrical alto, recalls a tender moment with the drummer’s mother before she passed away. “I was in her room in her last days, and she rubbed my head. I’m a grown man, but I felt like an innocent child. There’s a special love wrapped in the touch of a mother of every living creature. That special euphoria only comes from her.” The bittersweet “Wings and Roots” looks to the next generation, referring to Riley’s philosophy of raising children: “You have to root them in good values and fundamental characteristics, but once they get to be a certain age, you have to give them the wings to be free, to go out and be themselves.” Finally, “Stella By Starlight” is another nod to the American Songbook, taken at a graceful midtempo pace with Cohen’s deft touch over Riley’s sensitive brushwork. In the end, Riley hopes that the music of Perpetual Optimism helps spread the upbeat manifesto that he’s chosen to live by. “I always look forward, no matter what happens in life. If you’re grieving or faced with an emotional challenge, keep in mind: If you’re still breathing, there’s a chance that you can overcome and thrive. Commit yourself to PERPETUAL OPTIMISM!”

As an element of self attunement, we will practice making intuitive choices through a lens of self love, meaning that we are each making choices that are nourishing and responsive to ourselves as individuals in that moment. Part of this practice includes being very intentional and explicit about what kinds of choices we might consider, and being curious about how it feels to try them. Movements will be simple enough to follow along, giving us a chance to get out of our heads and drop into our bodies, regulating our nervous system. Movement Explorations: We'll explore movements that deepen our connection with our bodies and our intuition, focusing on concepts and areas of the body that can help us settle and release. Meditation: Finally, we'll settle into meditation and rest. 681c41b7-1b49-4f96-bcf3-73920e33e8dd: A somatic workshop to understand your nervous system, reconnect with your body, and learn practical tools for real transformation... Have you ever known exactly what you "should" do, but still found yourself stuck in the same patterns? Maybe you've read the books, listened to the podcasts, journaled, reflected, and tried to think your way into change. Yet anxiety, overwhelm, self-sabotage, emotional reactivity, procrastination, or feeling disconnected from yourself keep showing up. That's because lasting transformation doesn't happen through the mind alone. It happens through the body. In this immersive workshop, you'll learn the foundations of somatic healing and nervous system regulation, and why working with your body is often the missing piece when it comes to creating meaningful, sustainable change. We'll explore how stress, emotions, beliefs, and protective patterns are stored in the body, and why healing becomes more effective when we include the nervous system in the process. You'll learn: What somatics actually is (and why it's becoming more popular) Why mindset work alone isn't enough to create real, lasting change How your nervous system influences your emotions, behaviors, and daily experiences Simple somatic tools you can use to feel more grounded, present, and connected How to work with your body instead of constantly trying to push through or override it This workshop isn't just educational — you'll also experience somatics firsthand through guided practices, including breathwork, body awareness, grounding exercises, mindful movement, and embodiment practices designed to help you reconnect with yourself and your body's wisdom. You'll leave with: A clear understanding of what somatic healing is and how it works Practical tools you can immediately integrate into daily life to finally feel more calm and present Greater awareness of your nervous system and stress responses Simple ways to deepen your connection to your body, emotions, and intuition A new approach to personal growth that feels supportive, sustainable, and effective Whether you're completely new to somatics or looking to deepen your understanding of holistic healing, this workshop will give you a strong foundation and simple practices you can return to anytime! Please bring a journal and water bottle, and wear comfortable clothes. NOTE: Please be on time for this session — doors will close promptly and there will be NO LATE ENTRIES! About Anna Bolender: Anna Bolender is a certified Somatic Embodiment & Intuitive Life Coach, Somatic Breathwork and Quantum Wellness Practitioner, Reiki Master, and lifelong student of holistic health and well-being. Through her coaching programs and workshops, Anna guides others to return home to themselves — releasing what keeps them stuck, reconnecting with their body and inner wisdom, and creating real, lasting transformation from the inside out. Blending somatics, energy healing, quantum wellness, and mindset work, she helps clients break free from self-sabotaging patterns, repattern their nervous system, and cultivate simple daily rituals that support a fulfilling, grounded, and aligned life. Anna’s mission is to empower others to feel connected, alive, and radiant — no matter what life brings. 97fb1247-6163-464b-8682-ab331b91d115: As workers and as parents, we all care deeply about how we must prepare ourselves and our children for fulfilling careers at a time when the changing nature of labor is opaque. In this interactive book talk, co-author Illah Nourbakhsh will share brief remarks regarding our voyage in researching and writing a book about careers, AI and the future of education. We will be joined by two special pioneers who will make brief remarks from the audience: Alan Eustace and Professor Michael Genesereth. Alan Eustace served as senior vice president at Google and has witnessed the digital and AI technology revolutions firsthand. Michael Genesereth is faculty at Stanford University and charted the course of artificial intelligence research as one of its founding scholars. Both Alan and Michael care deeply about the next generation, and the ways in which careers will evolve as AI changes the shape of work. We look forward to a dynamic conversation with the audience. Featuring curated essays from leaders in tech and education, Crunch Time empowers parents, educators, students, and professionals to get informed and access their agency in the AI age. The AI revolution is underway, and none of us are fully prepared. In Crunch Time , education and AI experts Illah Nourbakhsh and Michael Druckman confront one of the central questions of our time: How will artificial intelligence reshape careers, education, and opportunity, and what should we do about it now? Rather than predicting a single future, Crunch Time presents AI as a dynamic, uncertain force that demands informed participation. Originally conceived for educators and parents, the book expands its lens to include students, alumni, mid-career professionals, employers, policymakers, and anyone navigating work and learning in the age of AI. Crunch Time weaves together perspectives from AI inventors, business leaders, educators, technologists, and community leaders, featuring more than forty contributors including AI experts Daniela Rus, Hoda Heidari, Michael Genesereth, Sanjay Sarma, university presidents Nancy Cantor, Lisa Ryerson, Laura Walker, Juan Salgado; business leaders David Siegel, Steve Malony, Dan Draper; visionaries Dame Diane Coyle, William Haseltine, Paul LeBlanc; and leading K to 12 educators. Readers will encounter competing viewpoints, practical guidance, and concrete steps for action. Crunch Time is an invitation to understand, to prepare, and to actively shape a more equitable and human-centered AI future. This timely and empowering book is essential reading for students, parents, educators and leaders who wish to shape an AI future that expands opportunity and strengthens our shared humanity. — Farnam Jahanian, President, Carnegie Mellon University For a book about artificial intelligence, this is brimming with human intelligence. You'll find thoughtful, nuanced, and provocative strategies for growing up and thriving in the age of AI. This book challenges us to redesign the connection between education and employment with intention and courage. This is a powerful call to ensure the AI age expands opportunity and strengthens pathways to meaningful work for all. — Lisa Marsh Ryerson, President, Southern New Hampshire University Our youth are growing up in the middle of a massive transition into the age of AI. Smart guides are critical to navigating this rough terrain, and this book is one of those guides. It elevates the power of human intellect and creativity, providing much-needed guidance on how to harness new technologies for the good of society and humanity. — Lisa Guernsey, Senior Director of Birth-12th Grade Policy, New America Illah R.
